longterm_thesis:
One cumulative thesis runs through every brief since mid-September: the marginal dollar of human demand — and therefore of capital — is migrating from convenience to security, and from asset-light claims on the future to physical chokepoints that are hard to build. Households are buying guaranteed electrons, resilient supply, fraud protection, restored physical function, and above all reclaimed time; corporates are buying the same things in industrial form (behind-the-meter generation, sovereign/on-prem AI, cyber tooling, domestic materials processing). A ~5% risk-free rate with $365tn of global debt is the regime, not an anomaly, which means the discount rate permanently penalises business models whose moat was cheap capital (marginal housing, levered consumer, REIT roll-ups, second-tier AI capex) and rewards owners of cash-generative constraints.

The single most durable, repeatedly-restamped observation across all five briefs is that electricity — not GPUs — is the binding constraint on AI. Amazon's $8B Generac deal, Meta funding seven gas plants, Mitsui contracting LNG explicitly for data centres, Italy reversing a 40-year nuclear ban, Duke and Constellation guiding 2026 higher: energy and compute are converging into a single asset class. This is the highest-confidence multi-year channel we have (0.75–0.8 in the source claims) and it is the one place where narrative scores are very high (power-demand 85, grid 77, LNG 75) while pricing scores are low (34, 55, 56) — the market talks about it far more than it pays for it. The second most durable shift is that people buy AI as time, not intelligence: 'ai phone assistant', 'ai phone answering service', 'ai agent builder' are the fastest-rising consumer queries, and enterprises pay for measurable labour substitution while punishing per-seat pricing. That favours incumbents with distribution and workflow data (Microsoft, Intuit, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Palantir) and devices/silicon that run inference locally (Apple, Qualcomm, TXN), and makes the terminal value of pure centralized compute rental contestable even as near-term order books boom.

The third axis is bodily and financial self-defence. Health demand is bifurcating: pharmacological metabolic management on one side (Lilly gaining GLP-1 share), and procedures/devices on the other — the 107% surge in robotic-surgery queries spanning hysterectomy, hernia, prostate and knee is an ageing cohort shopping for restored function, which raises the bar for CGM franchises to prove incremental value. Financially, a demographic-scale need for advice, custody, fraud protection and multi-venue/multi-currency access is forming (aging parents, estate plans, scam clusters, tokenised 24/7 settlement, Texas Stock Exchange, Indian retail brokerage) — the intermediation layer wins whether the underlying assets do or not. Housing is the clearest example of a need that will NOT be resolved: 7.45% mortgages freeze turnover, behaviour adapts into repair-and-stay-put, smaller units, rental permanence and multigenerational households. That is bearish turnover-linked consumption and bullish MRO/renovation for years — and the attention data (LOW, HD, SHW, LEN all in the not-priced bucket) says the market hasn't marked it.

Positioning implication: own constraint owners and toll roads on power, memory, optics, copper, skilled trades and workflow data; be selective in the crowded, well-priced parts of AI (CRWD at 89 pricing, PANW 84, AMD 79 have negative gaps — the theme is right, the entry is not); and accept that the AI drawdown, when it comes, will be a financing event (circular vendor financing: Nvidia into Anthropic, vendor-linked cloud commitments) rather than a demand event — which means the physical suppliers with contracted backlogs survive it better than the equity-funded compute landlords.

memo.summary: We are running a barbell that is only half-invested: 47% equity against a 66% recommended posture, with 26.8% parked in cash/T-bills after five forced exits (AVGO on trend-template failure, BAC/DXCM/NEM/SCCO on rotation thesis breaks). What is left is two bets and a rounding error. Bet one is AI capex duration — MU and NVDA at 12.8% combined, both stage-2 uptrends, both scoring reality 81 against pricing 52-56, supported by Technology being the single sector with accelerating flows (+66 rotation) and growth leading value by 96 points. Bet two is energy cash-return — EOG/COP/OXY at 21% of book, bought on a +84 Energy rotation score that has since collapsed to +27 with all three names carrying negative 6-month relative strength (-22 to -29) and the LNG theme trend fading 58 to 51. The regime backdrop is genuinely undecided (Goldilocks 26.6 / Contraction 25.4 / Reflation 24.6 / Stagflation 23.5) with Contraction the fastest-rising probability (+6.5) and Reflation the fastest-falling (-7.4) — which is exactly the wrong drift for the energy sleeve and argues the cash is doing more work than the stated 1.11 beta target implies. Realized book beta is materially below target because a third of the portfolio is in bills. Weighted expectations gap is a thin 17 points and weighted conviction across the book is low (three of seven names score under 30), so this is a trend-and-flow portfolio wearing fundamental clothing.

key_bets.why: Largest conviction score in the book (47.3) and the strongest technical/RS profile (RS 185, technical 100/8). TTM revenue +167%, operating margin +4,304bps, ROIC 74.5%, net cash $20.3B. But the thesis explicitly rejects the engine's 'cheap at 24x P/E' input — EV/Sales at 13.3x is the 77th percentile of history. This is a duration bet on HBM contracts and three-player supply discipline holding gross margin above 60% for 4-6 more quarters, not a value re-rating. Own it as high-beta cyclical with a hard 9.1% stop.

Revenue +83.4% and accelerating +12.7pts, operating margin +712bps, $127B FCF — against a 28x P/E sitting at the 0th percentile of its own 5-year range versus a 63x median. The 26-point reality-vs-pricing gap is the entire trade: the market is already paying for deceleration that the data does not show. Underwrite the two blemishes explicitly — 65.8% FCF conversion (~$58B of income not converting to cash) and incremental ROIC of 45.3% versus 113.7% trailing.

Highest-quality energy name we own (ROIC 22.1%, net debt/EBITDA 0.2x, share count -3.5%, 33x interest coverage) and the only holding flagged 'attention rising, not yet priced' (attention 76, gap 23). We do NOT own the 'priced for stagnation' framing — P/E at the 83rd percentile of its own range says otherwise. Edge is buyback compounding plus commodity optionality. Note the stated data concern: $580m capex on $27bn revenue is not a plausible E&P reinvestment rate, so the FCF yield is likely overstated.

New 5% position and our only expression of the top-starred theme (AI Software & Agents, trend 72, pricing 53). Revenue +78.9% and accelerating, operating margin +2,624bps, FCF margin 54.6%, incremental ROIC 500%, zero debt. The bull case is growth outrunning a still-extreme multiple, not multiple expansion — at 153x earnings and a 0.7% FCF yield, one quarter of deceleration re-rates it violently. Sized at 5% for that reason.

New 5%. Revenue -20.2% but operating margin +1,206bps, net income 2.0x, net debt/EBITDA down to 0.7x — portfolio pruning, not demand destruction. Lowest quality score in the book (36) and diluted shares +1.8% against 0.2% buyback yield, so shareholder return is currently being eaten by dilution. Conviction is 11.0. This is a cash-flow optionality tail, not a core position.

Candidly, the weakest entry this week and the one I'd flag hardest. Conviction 5.0, gap 2.0, LT theme conviction 0.42 (the only sub-1.0 multiplier in the book). Its own written exit rules are already live at entry: Financials rotation is -73 (threshold -20), Digital Payments theme trend is 39 (threshold 45), and operating margin change is -2.56% (threshold -2%). We sold BAC this same week for precisely the -73 Financials rotation print. The only defense is the ~15.2% shareholder yield supporting EPS compounding and a 7-criteria stage-2 technical. Expect this to be recalibrated out.

concentrations: AI capex as a single factor: MU + NVDA = 12.8% of total book, 27% of equity, both same sector and same theme, both levered to the same hyperscaler spending line. Their correlation in a drawdown is near one.

Energy at 21% of book and 45% of equity across EOG/COP/OXY — one commodity, one theme (LNG & Energy Security), three names with negative 6-month RS. This is the largest single-factor exposure we carry.
Cash at 26.8% is itself the third-largest position and the de facto macro hedge. Equity at 47% versus 66% recommended means we are structurally short the stated risk posture.
Growth/momentum factor tilt: growth leading value by 96 points, and our two highest-weight equities score growth 99 and 94. Small-cap flows are negative and we own none — that part is aligned.

Theme coverage is thin outside the top two: Defense Modernization 1.5%, Edge AI 1.0%, Robotics 0.5%, Autonomous Transport 0.5%. And we hold zero exposure to the second starred theme, Advertising & Attention Platforms (trend 55, pricing 40) — the cheapest starred theme on the board.

Valuation-percentile risk is shared across the book: MU (EV/Sales 77th pct), EOG (P/E 83rd pct), OXY (EV/Sales 93rd pct), V (76th pct), PLTR (153x earnings). Only NVDA is genuinely cheap against its own history.
biggest_risks: Memory cycle roll. The MU thesis states the downside plainly: if HBM pricing cracks, 24x becomes 8x on halved EPS. At 8% weight with 4.14% ATR and a 9.1% stop distance, a gap-down through the stop is a real 6-8% book event.

The Energy sleeve's entry condition has already half-decayed. Rotation went +84 at entry to +27 now; theme trend 58 to 51. Nothing has triggered an exit rule yet, but we are holding 21% of the book on a rotation score that has fallen 57 points in two weeks, with all three names showing negative relative strength. This is the position most likely to be wrong and slowest to be told so by the rules.

Contraction probability rising +6.5 to 25.4 while Reflation falls -7.4. A genuine growth scare hits the energy sleeve (demand) and the AI sleeve (capex deferral) simultaneously — our two bets are not diversifying against each other in that state.

V was bought with three of its own exit conditions already satisfied. Either the entry screen and the exit screen are reading different snapshots, or the rotation input is stale. Until that is reconciled, treat any Financials entry as suspect.

Data integrity in the energy names. The theses flag it three times: EOG capex implausibly low, COP's FCF computed as OCF with capex missing (so the 14.1% FCF yield and 7.1x P/FCF are overstated), and V's reported 7.8x P/E internally inconsistent with $22.2bn net income. Where valuation drives the gap score, the gap score is unreliable.

Cash drag if the tape rips. 26.8% in bills against a 1.11 beta target means we underperform meaningfully in a Goldilocks resolution — the probability that rose +3.8 this window. We are positioned for the regime that is falling, not the one that is rising.
Low-conviction names carrying real weight. COP at conviction 14.6, OXY at 11.0, V at 5.0 together hold 18% of book. These were not sized by conviction; they were sized by slot.
Long-duration Treasury flows decreasing while we hold 4.66% TLT plus 6.99% IEF — the fixed-income sleeve is fighting the flow data.
what_would_change_our_mind: Energy rotation printing below -20 for two consecutive runs — that mechanically clears EOG, COP and OXY and takes 21% of book to cash. Watch it; it has fallen from +84 to +27 already.
LNG & Energy Security theme trend breaking 45 (now 51, down from 58). Same effect, different trigger.
Technology rotation reversing from +66. It is the only sector with accelerating flows and it is carrying 21% of our book plus the entire watchlist.

Adverse regime probability (Stagflation + Contraction) crossing 55. It reads 48.9 now and was 53.2 at the original entries. Crossing 55 fires the regime exit on every single holding simultaneously — this is the portfolio's one genuine correlated kill-switch and it is ~6 points away.
AI Infrastructure theme trend below 45 (now 56). Would clear MU and NVDA together.

MU operating margin change turning negative YoY, or revenue growth decelerating below 117%. Both are miles from the threshold today, but the margin line is the single most important number in the book.
NVDA FCF conversion improving back above 80% would materially strengthen the thesis; deterioration below 60% would argue the accounting income is increasingly notional.
PLTR revenue growth decelerating below 55% — at 153x earnings that threshold is not a warning, it is an exit.
Financials rotation recovering above -20 would retroactively validate the V entry. Until then it is an unforced error.
memo.hedging_note: The hedge is the cash, and it is oversized relative to intent. We hold 26.8% in cash/T-bills against an 8% recommendation, 6.99% IEF, 4.66% TLT, 4.86% GLD, 4.86% LQD and 4.86% DBC. Practically: the five forced exits this week (24.3% turnover) were not redeployed, so the book's realized beta is well under the 1.11 target and the defensive posture is accidental rather than chosen. GLD at 4.86% is now our only hard-asset exposure after NEM and SCCO were cut on the -87 Materials rotation — that sale was rules-correct but it stripped the stagflation hedge (23.5% probability) right as we concentrated into two pro-cyclical bets. DBC at 4.86% partially offsets, though it doubles down on the same commodity factor already expressed through 21% energy equity rather than diversifying it. The TLT position is held against explicitly deteriorating long-duration flows. If the next recalibration does not redeploy the cash, we should say out loud that we are running a 47% equity book by choice and stop quoting a 1.11 beta target we are not expressing.
watchlist: FTNT (Fortinet) — highest watchlist opportunity at 72, perfect 100 technical, LT conviction 0.78, and sits in Cybersecurity, the top-ranked sub-theme in the flow data (Cyber > Cloud > Software). The blocker is a 3-point gap: it is good and everyone knows it. Trigger: a pullback that widens the gap above 12 without breaking stage-2.

ANET (Arista) — highest LT conviction on the entire watchlist at 0.80 with a 100 technical. Gap of 3 again. Trigger: gap widening, or use it as the AI-infrastructure replacement if MU's stop is hit, since it expresses the theme with less commodity-cycle beta.

TER (Teradyne) — widest watchlist gap at 19 with a 100 technical score and conviction 23.4. Best risk-adjusted new-money candidate in AI infrastructure right now. Trigger: conviction above 30 or a confirmed entry setup.

CRM (Salesforce) — gap 13, LT conviction 0.76, technical 88, and it sits in the top-starred theme (AI Software & Agents, trend 72). Would diversify the PLTR bet within the same theme at a fraction of the multiple. Trigger: technical score to 100.
CRDO (Credo) — LT conviction 0.80 tied for the highest, gap 10, but technical only 75 and conviction 7.2. Too early. Trigger: technical score to 88+.

CVX (Chevron) — technical 88 versus emerging-stage setups in EOG and OXY. If the Energy rotation stabilizes above zero, CVX is the higher-quality way to hold the sleeve. If rotation breaks -20, none of it matters.

AMAT / LRCX — semicap at LT conviction 0.74 each, gaps of 8 and 3. These are the second-derivative AI capex play; they confirm or deny the MU thesis before MU does. Watch as signal even if we never own them.

Advertising & Attention Platforms — a starred theme at trend 55 and pricing 40, meaning it is the cheapest thing the system is pointing at, and we own nothing in it. No candidate has surfaced on the watchlist. Flag for the research system: we want a name here before next recalibration.

MSFT / AAPL — 100 and 88 technicals, but gaps of 5 and 7 and conviction under 20. These are cash-parking equities, not edge. Only relevant if we decide to close the 19-point equity underweight quickly and need liquid beta.
